data.description:
## Description

**What**: Modify `claude-safe` (in `agent-batch-lifecycle.sh`) and `harvest-worktree.sh` to refuse worktree removal when ANY of three guards fires: (1) the branch has an open PR with CI in flight (checked via a 3-tier fallback chain covering main PRs AND sub-PRs); (2) the worktree has uncommitted or unpushed changes (reinforces existing git guard); (3) the branch is in a protected list (`main`, `master`, `develop`, `release/*`). The `--force` bypass prints which guard fired and the PR URL when applicable.

**Why**: Today `claude-safe` and `harvest-worktree` can delete a worktree whose branch has an open PR with CI in flight, orphaning the work. With S1's per-sub-PR workflow, a session worktree may have multiple sub-PRs in flight simultaneously — the existing single-PR-per-worktree assumption is broken. The 3-guard design also catches uncommitted-state and protected-branch removal accidents.

**Scope**:
- IN: `agent-batch-lifecycle.sh` claude-safe path modification; `harvest-worktree.sh` modification; 3-tier PR-detection fallback chain (`gh pr list --head <branch>` → `gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/pulls` → `gh pr list --search 'head:<branch>'`); end-to-end test creating a session worktree with 2 sub-PRs in flight; the `--force` bypass output.
- OUT: New PR creation; CI workflow changes; the cutover migration for in-flight PRs at S1 deploy (separate concern).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `claude-safe` (in `agent-batch-lifecycle.sh`) and `harvest-worktree.sh` refuse to remove a worktree when ANY of: (a) the branch has an open PR with CI in flight; (b) the worktree has uncommitted or unpushed changes; (c) the branch is in the protected list. The refusal prints which guard fired.
  ← Satisfies: "claude-safe and harvest-worktree refuse to remove a worktree when ANY of: open PR with CI in flight, uncommitted/unpushed changes, branch in protected list"

- When this story is complete, the open-PR check uses a 3-tier fallback chain: (1) `gh pr list --head <branch> --state open --json number --jq 'length'`; (2) `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/pulls --jq '[.[]| select(.state=="open")] | length'`; (3) `gh pr list --search 'head:<branch>'` or equivalent. The check enumerates BOTH the worktree's session→main PR AND all open sub-PRs whose head branch is a descendant of the worktree's session branch.
  ← Satisfies: SC4(c) + Red team Finding #6

- When this story is complete, `--force` bypass prints which guard fired AND the PR URL (when applicable) before proceeding with removal.
  ← Satisfies: "Bypassable with --force which prints which guard fired and the PR URL"

- When this story is complete, an end-to-end test (`tests/scripts/test-claude-safe-multiple-sub-prs.sh`) creates a session worktree with 2 sub-PRs in flight, attempts `claude-safe` cleanup, and asserts refusal.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #6 (sub-PR context awareness)

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done requirement

## Considerations

- [Correctness] `gh pr list --head` matches the branch name WITHOUT the `origin/` namespace and silently misses PRs from forks (per gh/cli issue #6462). The 3-tier fallback is REQUIRED, not optional — if S1's spike confirms tier-2 (SHA-based lookup) unreliable for non-default-branch commits, tier-3 (search-based) is promoted to first-tier.
- [Reliability] PR-close between guard check and removal (TOCTOU) — guard re-checks at the exact point of `git worktree remove` to narrow the window.
- [Forward compatibility] Once S1's sub-PR workflow is live, a session worktree may have many sub-PRs concurrently. The check must enumerate ALL of them, not just the most recent.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO operator, worktree cleanup refuses to remove a worktree when an open PR (including sub-PRs) has CI in flight
